references.text: Balaam repeats the same instruction about seven altars, seven bulls, and seven rams later in the same chapter, showing a pattern in his sacrificial practice.
Balaam again gives Balak the same command to build seven altars and prepare seven bulls and seven rams, confirming this as a recurring ritual pattern.
Job's friends are asked to offer seven bulls and seven rams, the same number Balaam required, suggesting a traditional sacrificial practice.
David offered seven bulls and seven rams at the dedication, the same number Balaam required, showing the significance of the number seven in Israelite sacrifices.
King Hezekiah offered seven bulls as a sin offering, reflecting the use of the number seven in biblical sacrifices.
